assertions.name: C1_GGM_defines_no_charge_lattice
assertions.source: P1 CONFIRMED. Measured over the sectioned text of arXiv:2012.00062v3: 'charge lattice' 0, 'Dirac pairing' 0, 'symplectic' 3 (both §7, both naming Neumann-Zagier). The sigma are labels for asymptotic series; GGM equips them with no lattice and no pairing, so H as stated is untestable against its own source

assertions.name: C2_NZ_edge_block_is_exactly_zero
assertions.source: P2 CONFIRMED for BOTH 4_1 (N=2) and 5_2 (N=3). A·B^T is symmetric on the edge rows (the NZ symplectic theorem), so the antisymmetrization vanishes identically. The edge block carries no antisymmetric pairing at all

assertions.name: C3_only_antisymmetric_part_is_rank2_cusp
assertions.source: P3 CONFIRMED for both knots. The entire nonzero part of J is the (mu, lambda) cusp block carrying +-2, i.e. the NZ 1-cusped relation. It is a rank-2 object about the BOUNDARY TORUS, not a sigma-indexed lattice of saddles

assertions.name: C4_NZ_route_EXCLUDED_scope_b
assertions.source: The NZ datum contains no rank-3 antisymmetric pairing of any kind -- its antisymmetric content is rank 2 and lives on the cusp -- so it cannot supply an eq-(98)-shaped pairing at any index set. Scope-(b): the cited invariants are the NZ symmetry theorem and the 1-cusped relation, not a search

assertions.name: C5_KRSS_is_the_wrong_symmetry_class
assertions.source: arXiv:1707.02991v1 ('BPS states, knots and quivers') is the one held source assigning quivers to knots, and its quivers are SYMMETRIC (6 occurrences of 'symmetric quiver'; the paper defines it as #arrows(i->j) = #arrows(j->i)). eq (98) is ANTIsymmetric, so it is not a KRSS quiver matrix on symmetry alone. Recorded SEPARATELY from the D1 bean's standing 'do not resurrect the refuted KRSS open-sector route (det(K)=5)' -- that is a different claim about a different construction, and the two must not be read as evidence for each other

assertions.name: C6_the_missing_object_named_precisely
assertions.source: The missing object is a map from the three GGM saddles {sigma_1, sigma_2, sigma_3} to a lattice Gamma carrying an antisymmetric integral pairing. It would have to come from the 3d-3d correspondence (the flavour/charge lattice of T[5_2]), which is not held in the library and is not computable from anything in this repo. Until it exists H is UNSTATED rather than unconfirmed -- 'the Dirac pairing on the charges' does not yet denote anything

assertions.name: C7_CORRECTS_C6_a_second_route_exists_and_is_partly_in_repo
assertions.source: CORRECTION of this probe's own C6, made after the colour-cubic audit landed on main. C6 asserted the lattice 'would come from the 3d-3d correspondence' and is 'not computable from anything in this repo'. Both halves are too strong. ROUTE 2, never named: for a spectral curve Sigma the charge lattice is H_1(Sigma, Z) with its INTERSECTION FORM, a canonical antisymmetric integral pairing (standard Seiberg-Witten / Hitchin), which does not route through T[5_2]'s flavour lattice at all. And the machinery is partly present: 3 A-polynomial producers (figure-eight, trefoil, Borromean) plus a rank-3 spectral curve worked in-corpus (the colour cubic -- wrong curve for 5_2, right method). What is genuinely absent is narrower: nothing computes 5_2's A-polynomial specifically, and the live intersection forms are on SEIFERT surfaces rather than on a SPECTRAL curve (different lattice, same construction). NOTE: this assertion originally required ZERO intersection-form files and FAILED at 10 -- my own control caught my own sub-claim, and the correction is STRONGER than its first draft: the repo has BOTH halves of route 2. So the next step is in-repo work, not an ingest. NOT a claim that route 2 succeeds -- whether H_1(Sigma) is the right lattice for the sigma is exactly as open as route 1 was

description: qou-q9ih D1-b. Opens the charge-lattice rung left by dt_d1b_gabriel_route_void_source_verified_probe, which reduced the arrow question to one labelled hypothesis H (V=3, 3 arrows) with one test: compute the Dirac pairing on the 5_2 charge lattice. This probe goes to source that lattice and DOES NOT FIND ONE, by three independent routes, none of them a failed numerical search. R1: the paper that produced the datum, GGM arXiv:2012.00062v3, contains 0 'charge lattice' and 0 'Dirac pairing' -- its 2 'symplectic' are both in section 7 naming Neumann-Zagier -- so H's test has no referent in its own source. R2: taking NZ as the paper's own candidate, the antisymmetrization J = A.B^T - B.A^T of the rect gluing datum is EXACTLY ZERO on the edge block (the NZ symplectic theorem: A.B^T is symmetric), and its entire nonzero content is the rank-2 cusp block carrying +-2 (the 1-cusped relation). Measured for BOTH 4_1 (N=2) and 5_2 (N=3), so structural rather than an N accident. eq (98) is rank 3, so NZ cannot carry an eq-(98)-shaped pairing at any index set -- scope-(b), invariants cited are the NZ symmetry theorem and the cusp relation. R3: arXiv:1707.02991v1, the one held source assigning quivers to knots, uses SYMMETRIC quivers by its own definition, while eq (98) is antisymmetric, so eq (98) is not a KRSS quiver matrix on symmetry alone -- recorded separately from the corpus's standing open-sector det(K)=5 refutation, which is a different claim. What remains is named precisely: a map from the three GGM saddles to a lattice with an antisymmetric integral pairing, which would come from the 3d-3d flavour/charge lattice of T[5_2], not held and not computable here. Until it exists H is UNSTATED, not merely unconfirmed.
